title: Mildred's power over a noisy room
summary: She recorded less well than she sang live; Norvo recalls her silencing a noisy nightclub with 'More Than You Know'.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Although I do think there is a few people on records that never recorded as well as they were in person. I think Bix Beiderbecke was one. I think he played much greater than he did on records.
Uh-huh.

I think Mildred is one. I've seen her in a nightclub and noisy nightclub, going into verse from "More Than All You Know, and she hit that chorus, that place you could've heard a pin drop. Now what did she -- now what does she have to control and audience that way. Now you've seen that yourself.
Yes, I have. Yes, I have.
I'm not telling you anything that you haven't seen.
I know, I know.
And I've seen it happen in ballrooms, I've seen it happen in hotels --
Yeah.
She had that magic thing --
She had a great gift.
Of -- yes.
-- She had a great gift and she was heart
and soul in it, that's what does it.
Well she was believable.
Yeah, that's right, Red.
She marries the lyrics with the music in such a tight way and the word -- the phrasing that she did was good with it..
Yes.
That you believed her, you really did believe her.
So you experienced something --
Right.
-- while she was singing you experienced something.
She made you actually identify with her.
